speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a pruritic rash on both upper arms. To help narrow this down, can you tell me how long this rash has been present and if you've noticed any new soaps, detergents, or plants in your environment recently? Also, does the rash appear in a specific pattern, such as a line or a circle?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: That duration of five months makes an acute allergic reaction unlikely; instead, could you describe the specific appearance of the lesions, such as whether they are scaly, vesicular, or ring-shaped, and have you noticed any family members developing similar rashes? Additionally, when you bathe, do the lesions on your upper arms itch significantly more than other areas of your body?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Nummular Eczema (Discoid Dermatitis).

Given the five-month duration, bilateral distribution on the upper extremities, and the absence of systemic symptoms like fever or joint pain, this clinical picture is most consistent with nummular eczema. Please request a skin biopsy if the lesions are atypical or if there is no response to standard emollient and topical steroid therapy.
